drills.q: Best ask 100.02 with 300 shares, next 100.03 with 450. You buy 500 market. Fill VWAP?
drills.a: 300 @ 100.02 + 200 @ 100.03 -> VWAP = (300*100.02 + 200*100.03)/500 = 100.024. Slippage vs arrival mid (assume 100.01): 1.4 cents on 100.015 mid ~ 1.4bp - the cost of walking one extra level.

drills.q: Daily vol is 2%, ADV is 5M shares, you trade 250k in one day. Square-root impact estimate with Y=0.8?
drills.a: Participation Q/V = 0.05; dp ~ 0.8 * 2% * sqrt(0.05) = 0.8*2%*0.224 ~ 36bp. Note sqrt: doubling to 500k only raises it to ~51bp (+41%), not double.

drills.q: Serial covariance of daily price changes is -0.0004. Estimate effective spread.
drills.a: Roll: cov = -(s/2)^2 -> s = 2*sqrt(0.0004) = 0.04. Effective spread ~ 4 cents. Caveat: estimator fails if prices trended over the sample (positive covariance masks the bounce).

drills.q: Your passive buy at the bid keeps filling right before down-moves. Diagnose and give two fixes.
drills.a: Adverse selection / toxicity: informed flow targets your quote. Fixes: (1) markout analysis by regime/time to find when your queue gets picked; cancel or widen during toxic windows; (2) skew quotes with inventory/signal (Avellaneda-Stoikov style) and shift toward taker execution when signal decay beats spread savings.

drills.q: Signal half-life is 90 seconds. Maker saves ~1.5bp round trip but queue wait averages 3 minutes. Aggressive or passive?
drills.a: Aggressive: waiting 3 minutes for ~1.5bp while a 90-second-half-life alpha decays means most of the edge evaporates before fill probability builds. Rule of thumb: go passive only when expected queue time << alpha half-life; otherwise pay the ~1.35bp taker cost.

drills.q: A backtest claims Sharpe 3.5 with fills at bar-close mid, trading 2% of ADV per signal, 50 trades/day. First three things you check?
drills.a: (1) Cost math: 2% participation x sqrt-law + saved half-spreads x 100 sides/day vs gross return per trade. (2) Latency: signal-at-close executed AT close assumes zero drift toward your own alpha. (3) Adverse selection on any simulated passive fills. Only then look at purge/embargo/trial-count statistics.

drills.q: Why do PFOF wholesalers pay brokers for retail order flow?
drills.a: Retail flow is uninformed: near-zero adverse selection per fill, so wholesalers internalize profitably (earn spread net of required price improvement) even after paying ~$0.0005-0.0017/share routing fees. The regulatory controversy asks whether the wholesale margin exceeds retail's price improvement - different question from whether individual fills beat NBBO.

drills.q: Markouts show your buys drift UP +8bp at +10min. Good execution or something else?
drills.a: Looks like captured value (paid below subsequent value), BUT verify: could be genuine alpha leaking through execution (strategy works), favorable regime luck, or small-size venue effects that vanish at scale. Re-measure at target participation before concluding the desk earns its keep - impact regime shifts with size (sqrt-law).

drills.q: Flash crash: what breaks first in an Avellaneda-Stoikov quoting model?
drills.a: Stationarity assumptions: cancellation rates explode (liquidity vanishes in ms), arrivals become one-sided, vol jumps beyond calibration - inventory skews calibrated calm quote INTO falling knives and adverse selection hits ~100% of flow. Survivors pre-wire hard inventory caps, auto-widen triggers on short-horizon vol/imbalance, and pull-and-requote circuit breakers.

drills.q: Design question: building a smart order router across 12 lit exchanges and 6 dark pools, what are the highest-priority modeling decisions in order, and how would you validate venue-toxicity scoring?
drills.a: Priority: (1) venue scoring via realized-vs-effective spread per venue to detect toxic/adverse-selection-heavy flow, (2) configurable risk-aversion (kappa) per order matching actual urgency, (3) real-time recalibration of impact/volatility parameters to avoid stale-calibration failure during regime shifts, (4) routing/tie-break mechanics last. Validate toxicity scores the same way as any predictive model: walk-forward, leakage-free backtesting -- track realized spread per venue out of sample and confirm 'less toxic' venues actually show smaller price-impact components after the fact, not just at the time scores were computed.
